---
title: "Ablation Study: Orben 2019 (NHB) - MTF"
format: pdf
---

```{r setup}
source("R/_load.R")
```

This document contains the ablation study for the MTF multiverse dataset from
Orben & Przybylski (2019, *Nature Human Behaviour*). Every decision is fixed
to one option in turn, importance estimates are recomputed on the reduced
multiverse, and the resulting importance vectors are compared across methods
and across options of the fixed decision.

```{r mtf-load-data}
mv_mtf <- load_multiverse("orben2019nhb_mtf")
```

## Ablation Study

`mv_dim_y_variable` is one-hot encoded (via `expand_y_variable()`) for the
regression and FANOVA methods: regression needs a numeric design matrix, and
FANOVA's random forest cannot handle the raw categorical with its many unique
levels. DECIDE uses it as-is. The expanded per-variable importances are
collapsed back to a single `mv_dim_y_variable` entry.

This multiverse is ragged: 8 of the 13 `x_variable` choices were only ever run
with a single `y_variable`, so fixing them leaves `controls` as the only
varying decision. Those settings are skipped (see `is_usable_ablation()`), as
an importance vector of length one supports no correlation. The
`n_options` column of the summaries below reports how many choices each
decision was actually averaged over.

Note also that only three decisions vary here, so every ablated importance
vector has two entries and the Pearson correlation of a single setting can
only be -1 or +1. `decide_main` and `decide_total` therefore always agree.

TODO: Double check the validity of this multiverse's analysis, manye more things break here than in the others. For practical reasons this one also disables the total.

```{r mtf-ablation-run}
ablation_mtf <- run_ablation_analysis(
  mv_mtf,
  colname_metric = "effect",
  regression_mv_pre_process = expand_y_variable,
  regression_post_process = aggregate_onehot_importances,
  fanova_mv_pre_process = expand_y_variable,
  fanova_post_process = aggregate_onehot_importances,
  include_fanova_total = FALSE,
  cor_method = "pearson"
)
```

### Inter-method stability

```{r mtf-ablation-inter-method-table}
ablation_mtf$inter_method_stability_summary |>
  mutate(
    fixed_decision_label = if_else(
      fixed_decision == "full_multiverse",
      "full multiverse",
      fixed_decision_label
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    fixed_decision_label,
    method_x,
    method_y,
    mean_rank_correlation,
    min_rank_correlation
  )
```

```{r mtf-ablation-inter-method-plot}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.5
vis_inter_method_stability(
  ablation_mtf$inter_method_stability_summary,
  fill_label = "Mean Pearson\ncorrelation"
) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### Intra-method stability

```{r mtf-ablation-intra-method-table}
ablation_mtf$intra_method_stability_summary |>
  select(
    fixed_decision_label,
    method,
    mean_rank_correlation,
    min_rank_correlation,
    mean_abs_difference
  )
```

```{r mtf-ablation-intra-method-plot}
vis_intra_method_stability(
  ablation_mtf$intra_method_stability_summary,
  fill_label = "Mean Pearson\ncorrelation"
)
```
